meta.name: Prosody Engine — craft reference
meta.purpose: The craft knowledge the agent applies as TASTE on top of the deterministic rhyme_engine.py: rhyme types (so the agent can name and choose slants), metrical feet, the cliché-rhyme blacklist to avoid, and sung-vowel notes. The live rhyme/meter computation lives in rhyme_engine.py (CMUdict); this is the human reference and the agent's taste rubric.
meta.note: A browsable in-page rhymer isn't shipped here because it would need the whole 135k-word pronunciation dictionary inlined. Live lookups run through rhyme_engine.py; this browser is the craft cheat-sheet.

rhyme_types.name: Perfect (full) rhyme
rhyme_types.desc: Final stressed vowel and everything after it match exactly.
rhyme_types.use: Strong closure; can feel expected — the engine's 'perfect' list, ranked by frequency.

rhyme_types.name: Slant / near rhyme
rhyme_types.desc: Close but not exact — the ear accepts it. Umbrella for assonance and consonance.
rhyme_types.example: love / enough, home / alone, orange / sponge
rhyme_types.use: Freshness and honesty; modern pop/folk/rap lean on it. This is where the agent adds the most value.

rhyme_types.name: Assonance
rhyme_types.desc: Same vowel sound, different ending consonants.
rhyme_types.use: Soft, open connection; keeps momentum without a hard click.

rhyme_types.name: Consonance
rhyme_types.use: Grittier, subtler tie; good for tension or unresolved feeling.

rhyme_types.name: Multisyllabic / rich rhyme
rhyme_types.desc: Two or more syllables rhyme together.
rhyme_types.use: Signals craft and flow (rap especially). Captured by the engine's 'perfect' from the last stressed vowel.

rhyme_types.name: Feminine rhyme
rhyme_types.desc: Stressed syllable followed by an unstressed one (ends soft).

rhyme_types.name: Masculine rhyme
rhyme_types.desc: Rhyme on the final stressed syllable (ends hard).
rhyme_types.use: Punchy, definite closure — good for a hook's last word.

rhyme_types.name: Identity / rime riche
rhyme_types.desc: Same sound including the onset consonant (or a homophone).
rhyme_types.use: Wordplay and double meaning; use sparingly.

rhyme_types.name: Eye rhyme
rhyme_types.desc: Looks like a rhyme on the page but doesn't sound like one.
rhyme_types.use: Avoid when writing for the ear — it won't rhyme when sung.

rhyme_types.name: Forced rhyme
rhyme_types.desc: A rhyme achieved by bending grammar, pronunciation, or sense.
rhyme_types.example: contorted syntax just to land a rhyme
rhyme_types.use: A warning flag: if the line only exists to hit the rhyme, rewrite it.

meter_feet.name: Iamb
meter_feet.note: The most natural English rhythm; conversational.

meter_feet.name: Trochee
meter_feet.note: Falling, insistent; good for chants and urgency.

meter_feet.name: Anapest
meter_feet.example: in the DARK, on a WHIM

meter_feet.name: Dactyl
meter_feet.note: Tumbling, waltz-like; feels tender or nostalgic.

meter_feet.name: Spondee
meter_feet.note: Two hits in a row; slams weight onto a phrase.

meter_feet.name: Pyrrhic
meter_feet.note: Two unstressed beats; speeds a line up between stresses.

cliche_rhymes.note: The most worn rhyme pairs in pop/rock. Not banned — but if you land on one, either twist it or reach for a slant instead. The agent flags these and offers a fresher partner.

sung_vowels.note: How words FEEL in the mouth when sung — sound is co-equal with meaning in a hook. CMUdict is spoken English; singers bend vowels, so treat this as taste, not law.

open_singable.why: Most open, most resonant — easiest to belt and hold.
Bright and forward; carries in a big room.
Opens as it sings (ah→ee glide); emotive.
Dark, intimate, closes a phrase softly.

harder_to_sing.vowel: ih (IH) / ee (IY) on high loud notes
harder_to_sing.why: Tight, thin; hard to belt — singers often open them toward 'eh/ah'.

harder_to_sing.vowel: nasals + hard stops closing a held note
harder_to_sing.why: '-nt', '-ck', '-t' choke a sustain; put hard stops at the START of a word, not the end of a held one.

sung_vowels.principle: Land the emotional/held words of a hook on open vowels (ah, oh, ay, eye, oo). Save tight vowels and hard consonant stops for quick, punchy syllables — not the notes you want to ring.

engine_commands.desc: Only slant rhymes, filtered to a syllable count so they fit the pocket.
Machine-readable output for the skill to rank with taste.
Total syllables + stress pattern of a whole line.
Rough check of a line's stresses against a target meter.
